messages.subject: Slow Computation
parts:
I am trying to run a simple two-stage hierarchical model in which the sum of multipliers for each child comes from a common distribution (see stan code below), with 100 children (F), 6 lags (K), and 40 to 50 data points for each child (D ~ 100). STAN takes about an hour to finish. I am wondering if this is acceptable run time or my for loops is inefficiently coded.

regards,
Vishy



data {
  int<lower=1> N; // total number of observations
  int<lower=1> D; // number of quarters/months/days
  int<lower=1> K; // number of predictors (factors / lags)
  int<lower=1> F; // number of children
  
  int start[F];
  int sizes[F];
  
  matrix[D, K] X; // predictor matrix
  vector[N] y; // observables
}
parameters {
  vector[F] alpha; // intercept
  matrix[K, F] fb; // multipliers to different lags
  vector<lower=0>[F] e; // child level errors
  
  real gb; // group Beta
  real<lower=0> sigma; // parent level errors
}
transformed parameters {
  vector[F] sum_beta;
  for(i in 1:F) {
    sum_beta[i] = sum(col(fb, i));
  }
}
model {
  int st;
  int end;
  for(i in 1:F) {
    st = start[i];
    end = st + sizes[i] - 1;
    segment(y, st, sizes[i]) ~ student_t(sizes[i] - 1, alpha[i] + X[st:end,] * col(fb, i), e[i]); // child level regression
    sum_beta[i] ~ normal(gb, sigma); // common parent distribution
  }
  
  // hyperpriors
  gb ~ normal(1, 10);
  sigma ~ cauchy(0, 2);
  e ~ cauchy(0, 2);
}

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Slow Computation
parts:
That's relatively efficient code. The data has an effect
on statistical efficiency; the code's all you need to look
at per-iteration time.

Here, the only way I can see to make this faster is
to declare X as

vector[K] X[D];

and then replace X[st:end,] with X[st:end].

And pull this out of the loop:
> sum_beta[i] ~ normal(gb, sigma); // common parent distribution

to just have

sum_beta ~ normal(gb, sigma);

- Bob
